[Spoiler=Storytelling II, Mungurru e o Cuco]
Todos estavam sentados ao redor de uma fogueira, o mais velho segurava um cajado de madeira, os mais jovens ao redor do fogo, crianças e adolescentes o observaram com atenção, sentados em um círculo, ele começou a contar.
-"Agora ouçam-me por um instante, vocês já ouviram do mito do Cuco e da Píton?".
O velho perguntou, os jovens acenaram que não, e ele logo sorriu, e começou a contar:
"Em dias distantes havia um cuco(pássaro cuco) de nome Dyirimadhi,  e Mungurru, ambos ancestrais que existiram no Dreamtime, o pássaro queria se casar com a filha de Mungurru, mas esse rejeitou  e o pássaro se irritou e gritou com o píton.
[i]-Por que me rejeita, Mungurru![/i] 
- [I]Você não é digno de minha filha Dyirmadhi, e mesmo que fale o motivo, você iria continuar tentando.[/i]
O velho rosnou em resposta ao pássaro teimoso.
---Mungurru, em um dia qualquer, encontrou um oásis, e dele usou para descansar sob uma palmeira.
---Enquanto caçava, Dyirimadhi encontrou outros pássaros como ele, rindo de algo, ele voou para perto deles, e então  questionou :
-[i]Sobre o que estão rindo?[/i]
---Porém eles não disseram nada, apenas apontaram para um oásis próximo, e quando foi lá ver, o pássaro encontrou o velho píton dormindo sob a árvore, o cuco riu junto e rapidamente foi contar aos outros:
- [i]aquele deveria ser meu sogro, Mungurru, mas ele se recusou a dar a mão de sua filha a mim[/i].
---O cuco disse, e depois o silêncio tomou conta, até que ele teve uma ideia, olhou ao redor, e procurou por algo, e logo encontrou uma pedra, uma grande pedra.
---O passarinho logo levantou a pedra com todas as forças, até as nuvens, mirou no velho píton e então soltou, em seguida , a pedra caiu sobre a cabeça do velho e a achatou, Mungurru gritou 
-[i]AAAAAH![/i] 
--- E começou a se debater de um lado para o outro, ele olhou para cima e viu o cuco rindo dele, [i]ora seu...[/i] mas, ele não decidiu se vingar, Mungurru só queria descansar quieto, olhou para o pássaro novamente e rosnou, o que assustou a ave para longe. Diante dessa situação , o pensamento do mar veio na mente do velho, por três dias e três noites ele viajou em direção ao sul, exaurido pela viagem e dor, rastejou e rastejou, e finalmente chegou. Logo a serpente se enrolou no mar, após chegar lá porém, começou a tremer [i]muito frio[/i], Mungurru gemeu, e rapidamente emergiu do mar e foi ao norte novamente, esticou seu corpo, pelo cansaço, logo ficou parado lá na areia do deserto, o sol começou a subir, mas o velho não acordou, seguiu dormindo, e lá ficou até que seu corpo endureceu e virou pedra.
 A cabeça de Mungurru se tornou uma rocha que se encontra com o mar, Dyiirii é seu nome, a rocha é elevada, e achatada, com uma queda abrupta até o mar, um típico promontório, e se você ver uma píton algum dia e sua cabeça for achatada, lembre de Mungurru e Dyirimadhi, que foi graças ao cuco que um relevo marítimo se formou e as pítons têm cabeça achatada.
"
Quando finalmente terminou de contar, o Ngankaris olhou ao redor, as crianças e adolescentes vidrados na história, ele sorriu, feliz por terem gostado da história, e então agradeceu, e como forma de "recompensa", pegou um pote de frutas e distribuiu 5 delas para cada um.
[i]Então uma parte do mundo foi literalmente formada por um cuco orgulhoso?[/i]
Um dos jovens perguntou, o ancião passou a mão em sua cabeça enquanto colocava 5 quandongs em suas mãos.
[i]Exato![/i]
Ele respondeu a pergunta do pequeno.

Everyone was sitting around a fire, the oldest was holding a wooden staff, the youngest were around the fire, children and teenagers watched him attentively, sitting in a circle, he began to tell.
-"Now listen to me for a moment, have you ever heard of the myth of the Cuckoo and the Python?". The old man asked, the young men shook their heads, and he soon smiled and began to tell:
"In distant days there was a cuckoo named Dyirimadhi, and Mungurru, both ancestors who existed in the Dreamtime, the bird wanted to marry Mungurru's daughter, but Mungurru rejected him and the bird got angry and shouted at the python.
[i]-Why do you reject me, Mungurru![/i]
- [I]You are not worthy of my daughter Dyirmadhi, and even if I tell you the reason, you would keep trying.[/i]
The old man growled in response to the stubborn bird.
---Mungurru, on any given day, found an oasis, and used it to rest under a palm tree.
---While hunting, Dyirimadhi found other birds like him, laughing at something, he flew close to them, and then asked:
-[i]What are you talking about? laughing?[/i]
---But they didn't say anything, they just pointed to a nearby oasis, and when he went there to see, the bird found the old python sleeping under the tree, the cuckoo laughed along and quickly went to tell the others:
- [i]That should be my father-in-law, Mungurru, but he refused to give his daughter's hand to me[/i].
---The cuckoo said, and then silence took over, until he had an idea, looked around, and looked for something, and soon found a stone, a big stone.
---The little bird soon lifted the stone with all his strength, up to the clouds, aimed at the old python and then let go, then the stone fell on the old man's head and flattened it, Mungurru screamed
-[i]AAAAAH![/i]
--- And began to struggle from side to side, he looked up and saw the cuckoo laughing at him, [i]oh my...[/i] but, he Mungurru didn't decide to take revenge, Mungurru just wanted to rest quietly, looked at the bird again and growled, which scared the bird away. Faced with this situation, the thought of the sea came to the old man's mind, for three days and three nights he traveled south, exhausted by the journey and pain, crawled and crawled, and finally arrived. Soon the serpent coiled itself in the sea, after arriving there, however, it began to shiver [i]very cold[/i], Mungurru groaned, and quickly emerged from the sea and went north again, stretching his body, out of exhaustion, soon he stood there on the desert sand, the sun began to rise, but the old man did not wake up, he continued sleeping, and there he stayed until his body hardened and turned to stone. Mungurru's head became a rock that meets the sea, Dyiirii is its name, the rock is high, and flat, with a steep drop to the sea, a typical promontory, and if you see a python someday and its head is flattened, remember Mungurru and Dyirimadhi, that it was thanks to the cuckoo that a sea relief was formed and the pythons have flat heads.

When he finally finished telling, the Ngankaris looked around, the children and teenagers were hooked on the story, he smiled, happy that they had enjoyed the story, and then thanked them, and as a form of "reward", he took a pot of fruit and distributed 5 of them to each one.
[i]So a part of the world was literally formed by a proud cuckoo?[/i]
One of the young people asked, the elder ran his hand over his head while placing 5 quandongs on his hands.
[i]Exactly![/i]
He answered the little one's question.
[/spoiler]

[quote=united_hydronia;59527119][b]Diplomacy[/b]
After weeks of back and forth letters and phone calls, President Kaplan Zorlu has finally made the decision to invite representatives of [nation]Vacan[/nation] to a meeting in the capital, Hydropolis, to discuss the possibility of a trade deal and mutual embassies.[/quote]
[b]Diplomatical Letter to the Government of the Democratic Republic of United Hydronia[/b]

Dear President Zorlu,

I thank you personally and on behalf of the Vacanian people for your invitation to Hydropolis. I am extremely pleased that our mutual contacts are now developing into direct and constructive dialogue.
The Democratic Republic of Vacan considers the United Republic of Hydronia a natural partner on the path to an era of innovation, stability, and mutual progress, therefor I will appoint a delegation of high-level representatives from the Ministries of Economic Affairs, Foreign Affairs, and Science to arrive in your capital as soon as possible. 
We enter this stage with an open mind, clear principles, in respect of our future partnership.

Anton Rayne
President of the Democratic Republic of Vacan
